correctness.rationale: Averaging an arbitrary projection over path-coordinate and equal-long-arm isometries preserves its range and norm bound; the invariant quotient is a single hyperplane projection with parameter u. The exact short/long column sums A(u),B(u) are proven for all u, the outer intervals are dominated, and the piecewise minimum follows by monotonicity and an explicit crossing. The Euclidean Gram projection uses inverse path lengths and gives r(a+b)/(b+ra). For a=2, b=2r the ratio is exactly r/2. The accompanying independent exact-rational matrix checker passed 28 instances; proof does not extrapolate from those finite cases.

value.rationale: Sharp infinite two-length series-parallel graph class, exact global minimizers rather than only orthogonal projections, a parameter-driven mechanism transition, and an unbounded r/2 ratio on simple unweighted planar networks. The latter shows graph Hodge projection norms can grow while minimal cycle-space ℓ1 projection norms approach one. This is motivated by graph transportation and invariant cycle-space projection theory; not a small isolated numerical improvement.
